questions.set_intro: Imagine that a friend calls to ask about your shopping habits. You talk by phone about shopping online.
questions.question: How often do you buy things online, and what do you usually order?
questions.model_answer: I buy things online about twice a month. I mostly order books, train tickets, and household goods that are too heavy to carry home easily.

questions.set_intro: Imagine that a friend calls to ask about your shopping habits. You talk by phone about shopping online.
questions.question: What do you check before you pay for an online order? Why?
questions.model_answer: I check the total with shipping and the date I can still return the item. A low price is useless if I cannot send it back.

questions.set_intro: Imagine that a friend calls to ask about your shopping habits. You talk by phone about shopping online.
questions.question: Some people want to see an item in a store before they buy it. Do you think that is necessary? Why or why not?
questions.model_answer: I do not think it is always necessary to see an item in a store first. For a familiar product, such as paper or a book, the description and a few reviews are enough. For shoes or a chair, I still want to check the size in person, because photos can mislead. So a store visit depends on the product, not on one rule for everything.

questions.question: Some people eat lunch at their desks. Do you think workers should take a real break away from their desks? Support your view with reasons and an example.
questions.model_answer: I think workers should take a real lunch break away from their desks. Staying at the desk usually means answering messages between bites, so the person never actually rests, and work done while eating is often careless. A short walk, or a meal in a staff room, gives the mind a clean break, and people come back able to concentrate. In my own week, the afternoons go better when I leave my screen for twenty minutes than when I eat over the keyboard. A team can still cover the phones by taking turns. The break is not wasted time. It is what makes the rest of the day productive, because a clear head in the afternoon is worth more than a few extra emails answered at lunch.
